entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 7_Iris_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 13970 vertices and 27936 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 199 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (20°, 23°), period 7.138843 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 101.9582450701366 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass. Re-read 2026-09-18: the release rotation record, 19.0414 25.8850 7.13884337, is the solution of Hanuš et al. (2019) read longitude-first, 0.1° from its Table 1 pole (19°, 26°); Table A.1’s (20°, 23°) is 3.0° from it. The display pole keeps Table A.1.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: Included 2026-09-18 as the SPHERE photograph lens: the 23 camera-1 deconvolved frames of 2017 October 10 and 11, the epochs Hanuš et al. (2019) published, cast onto the ADAM mesh with cameras computed from the release rotation record, JPL Horizons and each frame’s header. Its registration is the published comparison recorded in zimpol-published-comparison. The 20 frames of 2019 February and March are not used: the paper’s figure covers 2017, and a lens keeps one apparition. Earlier directory-level finding, kept: The live source folder https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/7Iris/ contains Deconv/ and Red/. Reduced and deconvolved observations therefore have a concrete archive route. Their pixels, image geometry, coverage and photometry were not qualified in this directory-level check, so these files cannot yet be treated as a registered global reflectance map. The current grid remains an explicit missing-imagery presentation.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 7_Iris_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked. Reopened 2026-09-18 because its condition was met: the photograph needs the mesh its rotation record describes. The SPHERE photograph lens rides this ADAM mesh, where the native outline residual is 0.84 px against 1.01 px on MPCD; the Shape and Elevation views keep MPCD.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Re-measured 2026-09-18 with the rotation record read longitude-first, which matches Hanuš et al. (2019) Table 1 to 0.1°; the earlier test below read it latitude-first, 9.4° away. The lens is prepared from 23 camera-1 frames of 2017 October 10 and 11 on the ADAM mesh and ships on its published comparison, zimpol-published-comparison. The registration stage reports: outline 9 of 23 scored, 6.83° RMS over a 1.98° floor, 6.54° systematic, all five 04:40 to 04:45 frames at −8° to −10°; frames reference decisive on 0 of 23; relief decisive on 23 of 23 at a 0.75° median; verdict conflict. With the record read latitude-first the same stage says registered, because every outline is too round to score and relief placed both readings within a degree. Coverage 47.4% of retained surface area over 5,920,363 interior texels, frame levels matched within 0.86 to 1.51. Earlier result, kept: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 16 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 5965 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.12 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.51; 0 of 16 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.6 as the registration of the SPHERE photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with tools/objects/published-comparison.mts against Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.6, the survey’s comparison of these frames with its MPCD and ADAM models. Outline overlap with the ADAM panels 0.957 to 0.979 at our phase; over a full turn in 10° steps it peaks at our phase in three of the four 2017 columns and 10° away in the fourth, by 0.004. With the photographs 0.964 to 0.983. Our own outline drawn again at the paper’s pixel scale scores 0.985 to 0.988 against itself, what the measure gives one shape at these two pixel sizes. The spin axis we project lies at 23.3° to 23.5° on the sky against 19.2° to 20.7° for the figure’s arrows. Turned in the image, our outline best overlaps the paper’s photographs at −1.5° to 1.0° and its model panels at −4.0° to −1.5°, so the axis difference lies between the paper’s own model and photograph panels, not between our cameras and the frames; its cause is not verified. Native outline residual 0.843 px mean over 23 frames, smallest at 0°. Earlier, against Hanuš et al. (2019) Figure 2: Our cameras reproduce the paper’s own comparison of images and model. Projected rotation axis 23.3° on the sky against the paper’s 23.9°, measured on its red axis line in all five panels; latitude-first gives 17.9°. Scale-free outline overlap with the paper’s image and model panels 0.980 and 0.972 at our phase, the single peak of a full-turn sweep in 10° steps, falling to 0.94 to 0.96 at ±10° and about 0.85 at a quarter turn. In the 23 native frames the outline residual after the limb-fitted centre is 0.84 px mean (median 0.83, largest 1.46), smallest at our phase and rising about 0.1 px per degree. The authors’ crater contours in their Figure 4, cast from native pixels through our cameras, put each of six craters on one surface point to 6.1 km RMS over 17 sightings, about 2.6 native pixels (8.8 km latitude-first). The paper’s phase labels count rotations from its first image, 2017-10-10 03:56:12, and agree with ours to the printed digits after that offset. Measured outside preparation with scratch scripts driving the pipeline’s own observerCamera, controlledShapeCamera, limbCentre and mesh intersection; the figure measures use the published figure, not native pixels. The paper states no phase uncertainty.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. (2019) Table 2 crater coordinates as registration controls
entries.finding: Projected as printed through the cameras that reproduce Figure 2, the six named craters land a median 139 km from the authors’ own contours in their Figure 4. No rotation or mirror of the table fits all six: a mirror plus 106° puts Xanthos, Cyanos, Chloros and Cirrhos within 1 to 18 km but sends Erythros about 190 km and Chrysos about 55 km off. Xanthos sits at exactly 0°, which suggests an author-defined prime meridian; the table does not state its longitude system. The authors’ contours themselves are used instead, in zimpol-published-comparison.
entries.revisitWhen: A statement of Table 2’s longitude system, or a machine-readable crater list in the model frame, lets the coordinates be projected directly.
